scripts.//generate: Prisma generates its client from an install script, and .npmrc turns install scripts off. Every entry point therefore generates it explicitly — chained with && rather than as a prebuild/pretest hook, because ignore-scripts disables this project's own pre/post hooks too. That is exactly how the first attempt at this failed: 206 type errors, because the client had never been generated.
scripts.//clean: nest-cli.json sets deleteOutDir, and tsconfig sets incremental. Together they produce a build that exits 0 and emits nothing: Nest removes dist, then tsc reads tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, sees no source file newer than its last emit, and writes no JavaScript. dist ends up holding only the copied assets. Clearing the build info is what makes the two settings safe together, so every entry point that compiles runs this first.
scripts.build: npm run generate && npm run clean && nest build
scripts.start: npm run generate && npm run clean && nest start
scripts.//start:dev: Cleared before starting for the same reason as build, plus one of its own: the watcher starts dist/main as soon as it thinks it is ready, so a dist left referencing a module the skipped emit never wrote surfaces as MODULE_NOT_FOUND for a file that is plainly there in src.
scripts.start:dev: npm run generate && npm run clean && nest start --watch
scripts.//install:wizard: Runs the first-run setup wizard. Starting it from a shell is the authentication: there is no administrator yet, so access to this machine is the only thing that can be proved. Builds first, because the wizard has to run before any .env exists and so cannot go through the watcher.
scripts.//admin:password: Sets a new password for a staff account, printed once. The seed shows the generated password exactly once and the stored form is a one-way hash, so without this a missed line in a deploy log locks everyone out of the panel permanently. A shell on the server is the authentication, as it is for the setup wizard; there is deliberately no HTTP route.
scripts.//start:container: The container entry point. Migrations run first because a deploy that starts an application against a schema it does not match fails on the first request instead of at boot, and `prisma migrate deploy` takes an advisory lock, so several replicas starting at once is safe. It runs dist directly: `start` is a development command that clears dist and recompiles, which would throw away the image's build on every restart.
